proposal: The Mandate recommends reducing DOL's budget to the low end of its historical average, using the Trump administration's FY 2020 request of $10.9 billion as a target, with the reductions made primarily in the Employment and Training Administration. status_summary: The administration has proposed cuts and consolidation, and the House Appropriations Committee has moved toward lower DOL spending, but Congress has enacted none of it. EO 14278 (signed 2025-04-23) ordered a review of federal workforce programs that could recommend consolidating or eliminating programs. DOL announced a shutdown of contractor-operated Job Corps centers on 2025-05-29, which a federal court in New York preliminarily enjoined on 2025-06-25, per VTDigger. The FY 2027 request would cut DOL discretionary spending to $9.9 billion from $13.3 billion, replace many WIOA Title I programs with a Make America Skilled Again block grant and eliminate Job Corps, per the National Association of Workforce Boards (NAWB). The House Appropriations Committee advanced its FY 2027 Labor-HHS-Education bill 34-28 on 2026-06-09; per NAWB it funds DOL at $9.8 billion, 27 percent below the enacted level, and its subcommittee draft cut WIOA Title I formula grants by 62 percent, while Bloomberg Government reports it again rejects the block grant and reduces rather than eliminates Job Corps. A WIOA reauthorization bill, H.R. 8210, cleared the House Education and Workforce Committee 19-14 on 2026-04-21 and had not reached the House floor in the sources read. A stopgap, H.R. 6500 (Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2027), was signed on 2026-09-02 as Public Law 119-103 and funds agencies through 2026-12-11, so full-year FY 2027 decisions remain open.

timeline.event: President signs EO 14278 (published 2025-04-28). Section 3 directs the Secretaries of Labor, Commerce and Education to review federal workforce programs within 90 days and recommend integrating systems, reforming or eliminating ineffective programs, and consolidating programs.

DOL announces it will begin shutting down contractor-operated Job Corps centers; EPI ties the move to a White House budget request that would eliminate Job Corps and cut DOL's workforce training budget by more than half in favor of a proposed state and local grant program.

After a temporary restraining order on 2025-06-04, a federal judge in the Southern District of New York (Judge Andrew Carter, per VTDigger) issues a preliminary injunction that keeps Job Corps centers open while litigation continues, finding DOL likely lacked authority to end a congressionally mandated program.

House Education and Workforce Chair Tim Walberg introduces the A Stronger Workforce for America Act of 2026 (H.R. 8210), a WIOA reauthorization with a 50 percent training requirement, expanded performance reporting and consolidation waivers for up to 10 states; the committee approves it 19-14 on 2026-04-21 and it awaits House floor action.

The administration's initial FY 2027 request (as summarized by the National Association of Workforce Boards) would cut DOL discretionary spending to $9.9 billion from $13.3 billion in FY 2026, create a Make America Skilled Again block grant combining WIOA Title I programs, eliminate Job Corps and eliminate the Senior Community Service Employment Program; DOL's budget page lists FY 2027 budget documents.

Bloomberg Government reports (month only; the first of the month is used) that a House Appropriations package rejects the $3.4 billion Make America Skilled Again framework for the second year in a row, cuts Job Corps by almost $1 billion instead of eliminating it, allocates $5 million to registered apprenticeships, and closes OFCCP, the Women's Bureau and the Bureau of International Labor Affairs.

The full House Appropriations Committee advances its FY 2027 Labor-HHS-Education bill 34-28; per NAWB, the subcommittee draft cuts DOL to $9.8 billion (27 percent), reduces WIOA Title I formula grants 62 percent and eliminates Youth, and the full committee left core WIOA funding levels unchanged.

The House passes a continuing resolution (H.R. 9770) extending FY 2026 funding through December 11; the Senate was advancing a similar measure, and full-year FY 2027 decisions were expected in late fall (per NAWB).

The President signs H.R. 6500, the Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2027 (Public Law 119-103), funding agencies through 2026-12-11; the Senate passed it 90-6 on 2026-08-08 (vote 228) and the House concurred in the Senate amendments 370-48 on 2026-09-01.

title: Cut DOL spending mainly in ETA and streamline federal workforce programs
uncertainties: Budget figures come from a workforce-board association's summaries (NAWB) and a Bloomberg Government article, not from the FY 2027 budget documents or House committee reports themselves; DOL's budget page was fetched but its PDF links were not visible, so the $9.9 billion, $13.3 billion and $9.8 billion figures are unverified against primary documents. The Bloomberg Government article date (approximately 2026-06-18) is inferred and the first of June is used in the timeline. The Job Corps orders are described through EPI and VTDigger rather than the court docket; the later status of the litigation was only reported as 'still litigating'. Appropriations and the Senate side for FY 2027 were not researched beyond these sources. The EO 14278 section 3 review report was not located. The two House FY 2027 accounts conflict: NAWB says the subcommittee draft would cut WIOA Title I formula grants 62 percent (Youth eliminated, Adult nearly eliminated by a rescission proposed for the fall) while the full committee left core WIOA levels unchanged, whereas Bloomberg Government says overall workforce funding is largely unchanged, so the final House position on formula grants is unclear. Any such cut would go beyond the Mandate's recommendation of consolidation and outcome-based funding, and the Mandate also targets ETA specifically, which the sources do not break out.
